post_title: Different layer fabric textures colliding
post_details: Every time I go to render this clo project the under layers fabric comes through the top layer. Is there any way to fix this? Please respond and help!

comments.comment_body: Hi 413120513853, Details aren't that well visible from this photo (a screenshot would be more helpful), but is there fur applied to the orange fabric? Then the hair is what is poking out, it is only visible in the render window.
It is a fur fabric applied to a garment underneath the blue one. It only shows in the rendering screen and comes straight through the top layer(the blue).
No matter what I do the underlying fur garment shows through the top layer, the blue garment.

Hi 413120513853 I see. When you are in the Fur Fabric Property Editor you will see three tabs under Materials. Front Side Back. For the Back (or whichever side is touching the shell material) Turn "Use Same Material as Front" Off. Then change the material from Fur to Matte. This way the fur is not only on the exposed side of the lining and will not Clip through the jacket
I thought that would help so I already had that done, but the bottom layer(fur) keeps showing through the top layer.

Dear 413120513853, In this case, it is the front side (if this is not lining but a separate garment, or the lining has not had its sides "flipped to normal" (3D window right-click command "Flip Normal")) of the fabric poking out. It would have to be set to Fabric: Matte there, but you could keep it on for the back. If you really want it to stay fur on top and not poke through anywhere, you can try setting Add'l Thickness - Collision of the furred pattern pieces up to a value that is high enough to contain the fur and keep distance to the next layer. However, keep in mind that IRL hair can be pressed down, which is not the case here, so it might not look as you intended volume-wise anyway.

post_title: Glueing accessories to a glove
post_details: HI! I have only been using CLO for a very short time and am self-taught. I could use some help. I have to glue those black pieces to the glove, but when I start the simulation not all the edges of the accessory are glued to the glove. How can I do this? The problem I think is the walls of the object, which being smooth, cannot adhere well to the glove when worn. Is there a solution?

comments.comment_body: Hi 20772003221529, Trims that are glued on only adhere to one point on the pattern piece, also, they don't have collision, so might be sinking in when simulation is turned on. Is this the hand pose as it should be in the final render? You can unglue the trims (right-click on them and find unglue in the menu), then they should not be moving anymore when simulation is turned on. As an alternative, you could build these OBJs as pattern pieces if you know all the measurements, add Additional Thickness - Rendering to them, sew them on, delete the seamlines' normal maps, and they will be moving with the rest of the glove without issue.

post_title: Im trying to make this garment non wrinkled...
post_details: Any time i simulate this model that I had created for me, it just collapses to the floor. There was no avatar when i opened the file either. all I want to do is make the garment non-wrinkled please help

comments.comment_body: Click on the 'show avatar' button in the 3D interface ( it looks like a head and shoulders - hover over and the first option along should be to show avatar) Then you can see if the file has a pre-loaded avatar or not. If there is no pre loaded avatar you will need to import one, if you simulate with no avatar the clothes are essentially floating in mid-air and so will fall down to the floor. When you bring in the avatar you may need to re-arrange the garments slightly to be over the avatar before simulation. If there is already an avatar loaded then I assume that the clothes are not positioned correctly, so again, after showing the avatar you will just need to move them over to be as close to the avatar wearing position as possible before simulating. Often the easiest way to do this is to select all in the 2D window, and then in the 3D window used the gizmo to move the outfit up / down / L/ R. Hope this helps

post_title: How to put a metal ring through eyelets
post_details: Hey. I am trying to make a metal ring that goes through eyelets and the fabric should hang from it. I can put it through the eyelets but when I simulate it, it looks like the second picture where it starts shacking like crazy? Does anybody know how to solve this? Thanks :)

comments.comment_body: This worked! Thank you so much!!

Hi 20719334742809, - The pattern pieces are colliding into each other upon introduction of gravity (turning on simulation). You can be able to prevent this by going down with both the Particle Distance and the Additional Thickness - Collision of all pieces involved: (Usually, it is recommended to choose a PD of 5 and ATC of 1 for high resolution, however, these eyelets and rings are so small, you can try with PD 0,8 (smallest possible value) and Collision Thickness of 0,5.) - For the metal pattern pieces, you should assign a separate fabric and choose the Physical Properties of Trim_Hardware for it. - You could also export the rings as OBJs and then add them in as hard objects, but as mentioned, the pattern piece only approach can be successful.

post_title: CLO Community Guidelines
post_details: Dear Users, Welcome to the CLO Community! We are glad to see you joining and are looking forward to your awesome posts!In order to sustain a positive, encouraging and inspiring environment within our community, we ask for your help and collaboration. Below, you can find a few concepts that we would like you to take into consideration while engaging on this platform. Respect: Everyone is welcome in our community. Every members unique perspective on things should be respected and accepted. Constructive criticism is fine, but dont be mean and disrespectful when expressing your opinion. Content that is offensive and contains nudity, vulgar language, graphic violence, or promotes illegal activity or self-harm is strictly forbidden and will be removed. Support: Dont hesitate to seek help. There is no such thing as a stupid question. We also encourage you to join in with our support team and provide help to your fellow CLO Community members. This is a dynamic platform where we exchange knowledge and help each other. Safety: Please do not share your personal information (home address, phone number, email address, user ID, password, credit card information etc.). Search: Before posting something, make sure to use our search function to see if the topic you are interested in has already been addressed. Often, the answer to your question is only one search away. If the topic is already on the table, you can always join the existing discussion. The search function is a great time saver for you and can help us avoid overlapping posts. Accuracy: Describe the topic of your interest in a meaningful way. Avoid using statements like urgent, seeking help, having trouble with in the Title field of your post. Rather, give a descriptive explanation of your problem/idea, for example, best practice for expressing realistic darts or human IK: how to fix a joint. Authenticity: Be honest and transparent. Post as yourself and dont hide behind a fake identity. All the content you want to share within our community should be original and owned by you or you should have permission from the initial owner. Be mindful and respect copyrights. Fun: Dont forget to have fun and get to know your fellow CLO Community members. :) In addition to these concepts, we have set some rules regarding self-promotion and third party services: We encourage you to promote yourself and your best work in the CLO Community. It is our pleasure to connect you with new and exciting job opportunities within the industry. However, it is forbidden to promote yourself by using other peoples work. If third party services can be beneficial to your fellow CLO Community members, promotion of these services is allowed. However, such promotions should not be in form of an advertisement but rather a helpful resource for others. We reserve the right to moderate posts and comments at our discretion.
